### CVE-2024-10382 — Arbitrary Code execution in Car App Android Jetpack Library
- Assigner: Google | Published: 2024-11-20 | Updated: 2025-01-06 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-502 CWE-502 Deserialization of Untrusted Data; CWE-94 CWE-94 Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 7.3 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:H/AT:P/PR:L/UI:P/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:H/SI:H/SA:H/S:N/AU:N/R:U/V:C/RE:M/U:Amber`
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

There exists a code execution vulnerability in the Car App Android Jetpack Library. CarAppService uses deserialization logic that allows construction of arbitrary java classes. This can lead to arbitrary code execution when combined with specific Java deserialization gadgets. An attacker needs to install a malicious application on victims device to be able to attack any application that uses vulnerable library. We recommend upgrading the library past version 1.7.0-beta02.

Affected:
- Google / Android: affected 1.4.0 <1.7.0-beta02 (semver)
- google / android: affected 1.4.0 <1.7.0-beta02 (custom)

Credits: Khanh Pham of Calif Hacking Team; Linh Le of Calif Hacking Team

References:
- https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/car-app#1.7.0-beta03

### CVE-2024-26131 — Element Android Intent Redirection
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2024-02-20 | Updated: 2024-08-01 | Max CVSS: 8.4
- CWE: CWE-923 CWE-923: Improper Restriction of Communication Channel to Intended Endpoints; CWE-940 CWE-940: Improper Verification of Source of a Communication Channel
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.4 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

Element Android is an Android Matrix Client. Element Android version 1.4.3 through 1.6.10 is vulnerable to intent redirection, allowing a third-party malicious application to start any internal activity by passing some extra parameters. Possible impact includes making Element Android display an arbitrary web page, executing arbitrary JavaScript; bypassing PIN code protection; and account takeover by spawning a login screen to send credentials to an arbitrary home server. This issue is fixed in Element Android 1.6.12. There is no known workaround to mitigate the issue.

Affected:
- element-hq / element-android: affected >= 1.4.3, < 1.6.12

References:
